 Curated by Suchitra Mandal , ET Online | Oct 26, 2026, 12:35:00 PM IST 1 / 9 DA hike July 2026: Why are central government employees still waiting?
 Central government employees are still waiting for the July 2026 dearness allowance (DA) hike. The government has not announced the revision even though the inflation data needed to calculate it has been available since July 31. Expectations rose in October, but the Centre did not announce the DA hike alongside recent bonus decisions or before Dussehra.
 ET Online 2 / 9 DA hike announcement: Why October 21 did not bring an update
 Many employees expected the DA announcement after the government’s Cabinet meeting on October 21. However, no Cabinet meeting was held that day. An official told ET Wealth that there was no meeting on October 21. This means employees will have to wait for the government to announce the July 2026 DA revision at a later date.
 Getty Images 3 / 9 Does the DA hike need Cabinet approval to be announced?
 The absence of a Cabinet meeting does not necessarily explain the delay. While DA revisions are generally announced by the government, the Finance Ministry can also make the announcement independently. Therefore, the government does not necessarily have to wait for a weekly Cabinet meeting to declare the July 2026 DA increase.
 Getty Images 4 / 9 July 2026 DA hike: Government already announced two bonuses
 The government has already taken decisions on bonuses for central government employees. On October 14, it announced the performance-linked bonus for Railway employees. On October 16, the Centre announced the non-performance-linked bonus for central government employees. However, neither announcement included the pending July 2026 DA hike.
 Getty Images 5 / 9 Why is the July 2026 DA hike expected to be 3%?
 The DA revision is linked to the 12-month average inflation index. For the July revision, the calculation uses readings from July of the previous year through June of the current year. Based on the average retail inflation data for July 2025 to June 2026, the estimated DA increase for July 2026 is 3%. This could take DA from 60% to 63%.
 Getty Images 6 / 9 DA hike history: How much did government employees get in recent years?
 DA increases have varied in recent years. The government raised DA by 2% in April 2026, taking it to 60%. Earlier, the October 2025 increase was 3%, while the April 2025 hike was 2%. In October 2024, employees received a 3% increase. The revisions have generally been announced around March-April and September-October.
 Getty Images 7 / 9 July 2026 DA hike: Employees’ associations protest the delay
 The delay has also triggered employee protests. The Confederation of Central Government Employees and Workers held a lunch-hour demonstration on October 16. In a letter to the Cabinet secretary, it demanded immediate announcement of the DA and dearness relief (DR) instalment due from July 1, 2026, along with the pending bonus-related announcements.
 Getty Images 8 / 9 When can the government announce the July 2026 DA hike?
 There is no confirmed announcement date yet. The government did not announce the hike during the October 14 Cabinet meeting, the October 16 bonus announcement or ahead of Dussehra. Since the Finance Ministry can also announce the revision independently, employees do not necessarily have to wait for another Cabinet meeting. The actual announcement date remains with the government.
 Getty Images 9 / 9 July 2026 DA hike: What will employees get if DA rises to 63%? 
 If the estimated 3% increase is approved, the DA rate for central government employees could rise from the current 60% to 63%, effective from July 1, 2026. This would mean employees could become eligible for the higher DA rate along with arrears for the period from July until the month in which the revised rate is implemented, subject to the government’s final announcement.
